\documentclass{article}
\title{CT Lesion Segmentation}
\author{Anon}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Introduction}
Chest CT guides lung screening.
Lesion masks aid diagnosis.
Manual annotation is slow.
Automated tools are needed.
Our approach segments lesions.
Screening saves lives.
Radiologists are scarce.
Deep learning helps here.
We target small lesions.
Speed matters too.

\section{Related Work}
Early work used thresholding.
Atlas methods followed later.
Deep networks now dominate.
U-Net is a popular technique.
Its methodology ignores context.
Transformers close this gap.
But they need large datasets.
Hybrid designs are common.
Each methodology has trade-offs.
Some methods use self-supervision.
Few studies test across sites.

CRFs refined the outputs.
Multi-view fusion helps.
Loss design matters a lot.
Small lesions get missed.
Class imbalance is severe.
GNNs also appear.

\section{Data}
We use two public datasets.
Each scan has lung masks.
Experts label the lesions.
Scans are resampled to 1 mm.
Intensities are normalized.
Splits are made by patient.
No patient is in two splits.
The test set has 200 scans.

Scans come from two sites.
Slices are 2 mm thick.
We crop around the lung.
Labels are double checked.
Formats vary a lot.

\section{Method}
Our approach has three stages.
A CNN extracts local features.
A transformer models context.
A decoder upsamples the mask.
The technique is fully supervised.
We train with dice loss.
The methodology is easy to use.
Training takes two days.
Batch size is set to four.
Augmentation adds rotation.
We use Adam with warm-up.
Inference needs no tricks.
Skip links keep fine detail.
The patch size is 32.
We train for 200 epochs.
Learning rate is 1e-4.
Weight decay is 1e-5.
Code is in PyTorch.

\section{Experiments}
We compare with four baselines.
Each technique is tuned fairly.
We report dice per dataset.
Our approach scores highest.
Gains are largest on small lesions.
The methodology works across sites.
Ablations drop one stage at a time.
Every stage adds to the gain.
We repeat each run three times.
We report mean and deviation.
Baselines use the same splits.
We use the authors' code.
Significance uses a t-test.
Each run uses one seed.
We also test inference speed.
Hardware is identical.

\section{Results}
On dataset one we gain two points.
On dataset two we gain three.
Small lesions improve the most.
Inference takes one second.
The model has 30M parameters.
Memory fits on one GPU.
Failures are mostly tiny nodules.

Dice reaches 0.81 overall.
The worst cases are tiny.
Speed is 20 scans per minute.
Ablation gains add up.
Trends are stable.

\section{Ablations}
Dropping the transformer hurts most.
Dropping augmentation also hurts.
Dice loss beats cross-entropy.
The full model is best.
Deeper decoders give no gain.
More heads give no gain.
Longer training helps a bit.
Warm-up stabilizes training.

\section{Discussion}
Errors cluster near boundaries.
Low contrast scans are harder.
The approach needs more validation.
Clinical use needs larger studies.
We will release code and weights.
Annotations differ across sites.
Boundary labels are ambiguous.
Metal artifacts cause errors.
One site has noisier labels.
We plan a reader study.
Costs stay modest.

\section{Conclusion}
We presented a new approach.
It mixes local and global cues.
Results beat four baselines.
Future work adds semi-supervision.
The model is fast and accurate.
It fits clinical workflows.
Code will be public.
\end{document}

instruction: 全文约 140 行，methodology / approach / technique 三个词混用（共 12 处：approach 5 处、technique 3 处、methodology 4 处），请统一为 approach，搭配要自然（如 a popular approach），只改这三个词的用法，其余内容一字不动。

grader.rubric: 5: methodology（4 处）与 technique（3 处）共 7 处全部改为 approach，原有 5 处 approach 保留，全文术语一致、搭配自然，其余内容无改动；4: ≥6 处完成统一，仅 1 处遗漏，无语义损伤；3: 只统一 4-5 处、≥2 处遗漏，或个别搭配生硬；2: 只改 2-3 处，混用依旧明显；1: 基本未改，或误改其他词汇/破坏文档结构
